What is the name and description of the business topic you want to create?

Please provide:
- **Topic name** – a short, clear label (e.g. "Customer Churn & Retention")
- **Description** – 2–4 sentences explaining what this topic covers, what business questions it answers, and who uses it
1.answer: Sales Bookings. Covers: Sales Bookings, Opportunity Product Mix & Pricing

selected.label: Sales Bookings
selected.description: Covers booking volume, deal-size ASP metrics (Bookings ASP, Addressable ASP), and closed-won opportunity data. Connects to booking targets and product-level pricing.
selected.ai_reasoning: Directly named as the primary subject of this topic — this is the root anchor node.

selected.label: Opportunity Product Mix & Pricing
selected.description: Captures the product-level composition of Salesforce opportunities — line items, quantity, discount, and pricebook entries linking each deal to its constituent products.
selected.ai_reasoning: Explicitly listed in the topic description alongside Sales Bookings; the graph has a direct 'informs' edge from this concept into Sales Bookings.

selected.label: Sales Targets & Quota
selected.description: Quarterly pipeline generation and bookings targets broken down by territory, segment, product group, customer type, and super-region.
selected.ai_reasoning: Has direct 'informs' and 'distinct-from' edges to Sales Bookings in the graph, making it essential context for measuring bookings attainment against goal.

6.question:
What business rules and definitions should the AI know for the **Sales Bookings** topic?

The suggestions below were inferred from your selected concepts, datasets, and metrics. Confirm, deselect, or edit each rule inline — then add any additional definitions your team relies on.

selected.label: A "booking" is counted only when a Salesforce opportunity reaches Closed-Won stage. Open pipeline, commit-stage, and best-case deals are excluded from all bookings figures.
selected.description: Prevents the AI from treating forecast pipeline or in-progress opportunities as booked revenue.
selected.ai_reasoning: The Sales Bookings concept description explicitly anchors bookings to 'closed-won opportunity data' — this is the root definitional rule for the entire topic and the primary distinction from the Sales Pipeline concept.

selected.label: Bookings ASP = total closed-won ACV ÷ all closed-won deal count. Addressable ASP = same calculation restricted to ICP-qualified (addressable) opportunities — non-addressable deals are excluded from both numerator and denominator.
selected.description: Ensures the AI picks the right ASP metric depending on whether the question is about the full book of business or the ICP-addressable subset.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both Bookings ASP and Addressable ASP are selected metrics whose denominators differ materially; without this rule the AI cannot distinguish between the two when answering deal-size questions.

selected.label: Bookings ≠ ARR. Bookings capture the signed contract value (ACV or TCV) at the moment of close. ARR is the annualised recurring revenue figure recognised after contract execution and is tracked in a separate topic.
selected.description: Guards against the AI conflating closed-won deal value with the ARR metric used in renewal and revenue reporting.
selected.ai_reasoning: A `distinct-from` edge exists between the Sales Bookings and Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) concepts in the knowledge graph, flagging this as a known confusion vector that must be explicitly addressed.

selected.label: SALES_TYPE segments bookings into New Logo, Expansion (upsell/cross-sell), and Renewal. Attainment targets and ASP benchmarks are set and evaluated per SALES_TYPE — always filter or break out by SALES_TYPE before comparing actuals to quota.
selected.description: Ensures the AI applies the correct target denominator when calculating attainment, since blended and per-type targets are not interchangeable.
selected.ai_reasoning: SALES_TYPE is a `segmented-by` column on the Sales Bookings concept, and the selected target datasets break goals out by customer type — mixing types would produce incorrect attainment figures.

selected.label: GTM Bookings (unverified) is the primary source for booking volume. Any figures drawn from this dataset should be treated as provisional until the data team confirms it is the authoritative table — surface this caveat in AI-generated answers.
selected.description: Manages the risk of stakeholders trusting unverified booking volume figures without context.
selected.ai_reasoning: The GTM Bookings dataset carries an explicit 'unverified' label in the app registry, indicating its authoritative status is not yet confirmed — the AI must reflect this uncertainty when citing booking volume.

selected.label: AVG Booking and Bookings Dynamic are archived (legacy) metrics. Default to Bookings ASP and Addressable ASP for all current reporting. Reference archived metrics only if a user explicitly asks for historical trend continuity across the pre-migration period.
selected.description: Prevents the AI from surfacing stale metrics when current equivalents exist.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both AVG Booking and Bookings Dynamic sit under an 'Archive' dashboard path in the metric registry, signalling they have been superseded by the ASP metrics confirmed in step 4.

7.question:
Are there terms in the **Sales Bookings** topic that could be confused with terms in other topics or datasets?

The pairs below were identified from `distinct-from` edges in the knowledge graph, shared column names across your selected datasets, and the business rules confirmed in step 6. Select all disambiguation rules the AI should enforce — deselect any that don't apply, and add any custom pairs your team has run into.

selected.label: "Bookings" ≠ "Pipeline" — pipeline covers all open opportunity stages; bookings are Closed-Won only
selected.description: When a user asks about 'sales numbers', 'open deals', or 'opportunities', the AI must determine whether they mean open pipeline (tracked in the Sales Pipeline topic) or closed-won bookings (this topic). The two must never be blended in a single calculation or answer.
selected.ai_reasoning: A direct `distinct-from` edge exists between Sales Bookings and Sales Pipeline in the knowledge graph — conflating open pipeline with booked revenue is the single most common error in sales reporting and the primary reason the graph models these as distinct concepts.

selected.label: "ASP" is ambiguous — Bookings ASP (all closed-won deals) vs Addressable ASP (ICP-qualified deals only) share the same acronym but have different denominators
selected.description: Both selected KPIs share the abbreviation 'ASP' but differ materially in scope. When a user asks for 'ASP' without qualification, the AI should default to Bookings ASP and surface a prompt asking whether they mean the ICP-addressable subset. The two metrics should never be averaged or combined.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both Bookings ASP and Addressable ASP carry `measured-by` edges from the Sales Bookings concept and were confirmed as active KPIs in step 4 — without a resolution rule, bare 'ASP' references are unresolvable by the AI.

selected.label: "Renewal" in SALES_TYPE (a closed-won renewal booking) ≠ the Customer Renewal topic (the pre-close renewal management process)
selected.description: Within this topic, SALES_TYPE = 'Renewal' identifies deals that were contract renewals at the moment of close — a bookings event counted in attainment. The Customer Renewal concept is a separate topic tracking the upstream renewal pipeline, CSM activity, and ICP prioritisation before close. The AI must not route 'renewal bookings' questions to the wrong topic.
selected.ai_reasoning: SALES_TYPE is a `segmented-by` column on the Sales Bookings concept; Customer Renewal is a distinct graph concept with its own datasets (DWH_RENEWAL_OPPORTUNITY, Product - Opportunities) — a question about 'renewal attainment vs quota' could be misrouted without this rule.

selected.label: The "Product - Opportunities" event covers ALL deal stages — a Closed-Won stage filter must always be applied before using it for bookings calculations
selected.description: The selected event stream (Users.Scott Levine.Product - Opportunities) tracks stage transitions across all opportunity statuses, not just closed deals. Using it without an explicit STAGE_NAME = 'Closed-Won' filter will inflate booking counts with open, commit, and best-case pipeline. The AI should enforce this filter automatically when answering questions in this topic.
selected.ai_reasoning: This event is composed by the Sales Pipeline concept (all stages) and tracked-in by Customer Renewal — its native scope extends well beyond closed-won deals, making the required filter non-obvious to users who query it through this topic.

selected.label: "Targets" in the selected datasets contains both pipe-gen goals (PIPE_GEN_GOAL) and bookings goals (BOOKINGS_GOAL) — these are not interchangeable
selected.description: Both SFDC_PIPE_GENERATION_BOOKINGS_TARGETS and SFDC_PIPE_GENERATION_BOOKINGS_PRODUCT_ANALYTICS_TARGETS store dual goal columns in the same table. A question about 'target attainment' must specify which goal type is meant. The AI should never compute blended attainment across both goal columns in the same answer.
selected.ai_reasoning: Both selected target datasets use compound names that combine 'pipe generation' and 'bookings' targets in a single table — the shared dataset name creates structural ambiguity about which goal column should underlie any attainment calculation.

selected.label: "Product" in this topic means Salesforce pricebook / SKU items (SFDC_PRODUCT) — not Optimizely's own product lines (CMP, Experimentation, Opal)
selected.description: When users ask about 'product mix' or 'product-level bookings', they are asking which Salesforce catalogue items appear in opportunity line items. Optimizely's internal product suite (tracked via PRODUCT_SOLUTION and PRODUCT_GROUP in ARR, churn, and engagement topics) is a distinct concept and should not be substituted.
selected.ai_reasoning: SFDC_PRODUCT is a selected dataset composed by the Opportunity Product Mix & Pricing concept; 'product' is simultaneously a high-frequency term across Optimizely's product engagement, ARR, and usage topics — cross-topic collision without this rule is highly likely.

8.question:
How should the **Sales Bookings** topic grow over time?

As the knowledge graph evolves — new datasets are added, concepts get new edges, and the AI discovers indirect relationships — this policy controls how automatically the topic expands to absorb those new connections.

Choose the expansion policy that best fits how tightly governed this topic needs to be.

selected.label: Moderate — 2-hop discovery, human-confirmed (depth 2, human-confirmed) ✦ Recommended
selected.description: The topic can automatically surface entities up to 2 hops from the confirmed root concepts, but each candidate still requires human confirmation before it is formally included. In practice this means the AI may propose: Sales Pipeline datasets (1 hop via `distinct-from` — useful for bookings-vs-pipeline context), Sales Rep Performance metrics (2 hops via Sales Targets & Quota → `informs`), and ICP Account Targeting columns (2 hops via SFDC_PIPE_GENERATION_BOOKINGS_PRODUCT_ANALYTICS_TARGETS). None of these are added silently — they appear as suggestions awaiting your approval.
selected.ai_reasoning: Moderate is the right default here because the Sales Bookings graph neighbourhood is dense with relevant concepts (Sales Pipeline, Sales Rep Performance, ICP Account Targeting) that provide meaningful context for bookings attainment questions, while the human-confirmation gate preserves the strict definitional boundaries established in steps 6 and 7 — particularly the Closed-Won only rule and the bookings ≠ ARR separation.
